title: Review prime's contract against how beads primes an agent
body: The contract paragraph says how to use each command and nothing about when, or that foam is preferred over a handoff file, a TODO comment or the harness's own memory. Gaps seen in one session: no prompt to foam create when finding work, no trigger or examples for foam remember, no trigger for foam note, stale memories are marked but nothing says to fix or forget them. Compare with what beads injects at session start and decide what the paragraph should say.

notes.author: Jack Roddy
notes.text: Three stores, three speech acts. A rule is an instruction: human intent, written or approved by a person, versioned with the code it governs, changed by commit and review; lives in CLAUDE.md. A memory is an observation: agent-written, unreviewed, true until the world drifts, which is why foam stamps it and marks it old; lives in foam. An issue is an intention with a lifecycle; lives in foam. Test for a borderline item: who is wrong if it is false? A human who set it: rule. The world moved: memory. Nothing is wrong yet but something should change: issue. 'Reinstall foam after a change' is a memory even though it reads like an instruction, because nobody decided it. Memories are the one prose store an agent writes without review; that is the design, not a gap. Promotion path: an agent remembers a fact, a human sees it in prime a few sessions running and makes it a rule or an issue. Memories must not duplicate CLAUDE.md, since both land in every session's context. Consequences for the contract paragraph: tell the agent to remember facts, never rules, and to say in its reply when a fact looks like it wants to become a rule. The contract is the one rule foam itself owns, which is why it lives in prime rather than in every adopter's CLAUDE.md. Also: the README should state this separation in the same testable terms.
